title: How many fold lines do these four shapes have?
description: A tilted square, an eight pointed star, a triangle with equal sides and equal angles, and a six sided shape with equal sides and equal angles are folded in the mind. The matching folds of each are counted.
teaching_notes: One idea: a shape with equal sides and equal angles has as many lines of symmetry as it has sides, and the star has as many as it has points. Watch for students who think tilting a square changes the number of folds.

source: How many lines of symmetry do these shapes have? (a) a square drawn tilted like a diamond, and an eight-pointed star shape; (b) a triangle with equal sides and equal angles; (c) a hexagon with equal sides and equal angles.
video_script.why: The child counts the matching folds of four shapes and sees that the number follows the sides or points.
video_script.substitution: Fold each shape in the mind and count the folds where the two halves cover each other.
video_script.anchor: Four shapes: a tilted square, an eight pointed star, a triangle with equal sides and a six sided shape with equal sides
video_script.payoff_line: These shapes have as many lines as they have sides or points.

final_answer.value: tilted square: 4; eight pointed star: 8; triangle with equal sides: 3; six sided shape with equal sides: 6
final_answer.spoken: the tilted square has four lines, the eight pointed star has eight, the triangle has three, and the six sided shape has six

never_show: the counts before the folds are made
a count written on any shape in the steps
maths_rules: A line of symmetry is a fold line along which one half covers the other exactly.
Tilting a square does not change its folds: it has four lines.
The eight pointed star has eight lines: four through opposite points and four through opposite notches.
A triangle with equal sides and equal angles has three lines, one from each corner to the middle of the opposite side.
A six sided shape with equal sides and equal angles has six lines: three through opposite corners and three through the middles of opposite sides.
Check: the number of lines equals the number of sides, or points for the star.
video_script.design: One idea: count the matching folds of each shape. Assumes the child has found the four folds of a square. The four shapes stay on the board from the hook to the end.
open_questions: The star is read from the worklist as an eight pointed star with its points and notches evenly spaced.
